note: He owns his own business, which is the literal wording of the occupation criterion, though a two-year-old carpentry company is some distance from the physician-or-equivalent example the ICP quote uses. Health is squarely the neglected area, and he is not the deconditioned exclusion — by his own account 'I've always been in pretty good shape... I've got a decent definition for not doing anything'. He fails on the other two: no income evidence was gathered at any point and a second-year trade business is exactly the profile where $6,000 is a stretch, and he is not going good-to-great but starting from zero — 'I've never seen myself as a person who works out'. Notably the criterion that actually decided this call is absent from the stated ICP entirely: readiness to commit. The rep disqualified on it, correctly, using a test the ICP does not contain.
